lines: Travel.
I've been dreaming about this since I was a kid.
Going into the unknown.Wandering off the beaten path.Making friends that don't speak my language.
I distinctly remember running around my auntie's house telling everyone I would see the world.
The excitement was electric.
I could feel the adrenaline hitting every single part of my body as soon as I stepped off that first flight.
Marrakesh.
My first stop.
I have never been anywhere this foreign.
The first walk through the Medina overloaded my senses
The smell of burning gasoline from the motorcycles burned my nostrils as they ripped through the streets.
The colors were so vibrant. Nothing like I've ever seen before.
It was chaotic.
It was new.
It was raw.
It was what I've always hoped for.
Alone.
You will never hear me complain about getting to travel. Any traveller around the world will tell you that travel is a privilege only few get to experience, so be grateful.
I am grateful.
But, solo travel was not what I expected.
It got lonely, it got tiring, and there were some days where I felt so drained that I didn't leave the hostel.
I miss my friends.
I've spent most of this past year alone. Moved to a new country for 8 months, then headed around the world.
When was the last time I talked to them?
Is it worth it?
A question I wrote down in my journal.
I only have so much time this summer.
What about family? What about career? Am I falling behind?
Am I wasting my time?
But we gotta keep going.
Stay in the moment.
Something that's so easy to say but so hard to do.
Enjoy the thrill, let the worries pass, and have some fun.
Keep it simple. Don't think too much.
Meet some people.
Like Tony said.
Say yes to everything.
Experience as much as you can and be grateful, for you are lucky enough to do it.
This trip was everything I wanted it to be and more. Both good and bad.
There were times where it wrecked me. Times where I just sat in a cafe all day writing in my journal, thinking what am I doing?
Turkish aunties that treated me to tavukgöğsü.
The Puerto Ricans that kept me energized on the cold mountain side of Mt Fuji.
My German friends helping me up after wiping out on a glacier in Georgia.
Came out of it more grateful, more excited, and more confident about life. Things I did not expect to get out of this trip.
An experience of a lifetime.
But now.. onto the next adventure.
